title: Jimmy Boyd Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Jimmy Boyd review, checked 7 Nov 2026: his real package prices, how the profit guarantee works, who grades his record, and what buyers report.

short_answer: Jimmy Boyd runs a real, working pick business. His site names an operator, publishes every price, takes payment through a SportsCapping checkout, and posts a dated archive of his graded picks. In that narrow sense he is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money over time is not something we could confirm. His record is graded and published by SportsCapping.com, and both SportsCapping and BoydsBets list the same contact: Boyd Information Group at the same Henderson address. His FAQ calls this documentation by "independent sports monitors", but a grader that shares the seller's name and address is not independent. His sales copy also mixes numbers, such as "nearly 20 years" next to a 2002 start date.

Treat the archive as useful raw data from the seller, not as an audit. If you buy, buy short, record every pick yourself with the line and time you received it, and judge it after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: Almost every short package is sold as "100% GUARANTEED!" and the BoydsBets buy page says all the picks on it "come GUARANTEED to show you a profit." The rules sit in the SportsCapping Guaranteed Pick Policy. If you do not show a profit during the paid period, you get an equal length subscription free. The policy says plainly: "We do not offer monetary refunds."

Read the fine print. Any profit, however small, counts as a win and ends the guarantee. Every pick is graded at a flat 100 units, whatever star rating it carried. You get one free term per purchase, even if the free term also loses. Season subscriptions carry no profit guarantee at all. The SportsCapping refund policy says products are sold "as is" and no refunds will be issued, though a subscription can be swapped for one of equal or lesser value. Losses on your own bets are never covered.

claims_note: The streak numbers start on dates the seller picks. On his SportsCapping page each row has its own start date: college basketball from 17 Mar 2026, top football from 24 Oct 2026, all sports from 9 Mar 2025. Starting each count after a cold spell is an easy way to make every sport look hot. "Dime bettors" means $1,000 a pick, ten times the $100 the board uses, so the sales copy figures are ten times the board's own: the college basketball row shows $1,527, while the sales copy says $15,270.

Some copy does not hold together. The 1 day pass is priced at $49.95, but its text says "For just $99". The 3 day pass text compares itself to "$99 for one day", and the 7 day pass text says "just $43/day", which does not match a $199.95 price over 7 days. The free pick section says "All plays are made using sophisticated machine learning models," while the About page has Boyd writing "I'm not a system player by any means."
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full pick log kept by a grader with no tie to the seller, no third party contest results we could open, and no court or regulator record about Jimmy Boyd or Boyd Information Group.

What the seller's network publishes: SportsCapping shows a Jimmy Boyd archive of 100 picks a page, with the date, the pick and line, the score, the result, the profit at $100 a pick and the lead time before the game, and it includes losses. On 7 Nov 2026 the latest day, 6 Nov, read 5 wins and 1 loss for +410. His all sports row reads 1335-1161, +$10,838, 53%, since 9 Mar 2025. On the SportsCapping current season leaderboard by profit, he was not in the top 20 shown. This is real, dated data, but it is graded by a site that lists the same operator, so it is the seller's own record, not an audit.

A note on our earlier edition: on 27 Oct 2026 a direct request for a SportsCapping export address returned "Invalid access", so that edition printed no prices. On 7 Nov 2026 both his BoydsBets page and his SportsCapping page opened and showed the prices above.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Jimmy Boyd is thin. We found one BBB complaint and no large review sample. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: A buyer told the BBB that a season pass bought on 5 Sep 2026 was never delivered and that four or five emails got no reply. The business answered that a system fault had recorded the order without turning the pass on, that it activated the pass on 29 Sep backdated to the purchase, and that it offered a partial or full refund. BBB lists the complaint as resolved, confirmed by the customer on 30 Sep 2026.

BBB lists Boyd Information Group as a sports handicapper, not accredited and not rated, with a file opened on 9/29/2026 and 1 complaint in the last 12 months. A new file means BBB has little history to go on either way.

His sales copy says clients "return each fall" and that more members return to his service every year than any other. These are the seller's own words, with no customer named, so they tell you nothing about a typical buyer.

Trustpilot showed no page for boydsbets.com or sportscapping.com. Reddit search asked us to log in, so we could not read it. We found no TheRX or Sportsbook Review forum thread about Jimmy Boyd with a real discussion of results.

conflicts: The biggest one is the grader. SportsCapping.com grades and ranks Boyd's picks, sells them, and runs his checkout, and its footer lists Boyd Information Group at the same Henderson address as the BoydsBets contact page. We did not find a document that says who owns each site, but a buyer should not treat SportsCapping's archive or its top 10 rankings as an outside audit of Boyd.
BoydsBets also sells picks from other handicappers through the same SportsCapping checkout, so the site earns from a whole roster, not only from Boyd.

His FAQ says a free trial is offered "only if you sign up for one of our recommended sportsbooks and make a deposit." The sportsbook page ranks offshore books such as BetOnline, Bovada and Bookmaker, and the FAQ says his posted line comes from "a variety of offshore books." On 7 Nov 2026 the Go to links we tested led to logo images or a review page, so we saw no tracking code, but tying a trial to a deposit shows an interest in where you bet. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live.
strengths: A named operator, an address and a full price list, the same on both of his storefronts.

A dated pick archive on SportsCapping with the line, the score, the result, the profit and the lead time before the game, including losses. Yesterday's Best on the SportsCapping homepage showed him at $410, which matches his 6 Nov archive rows.
Free picks with a full written case are posted daily, so a reader can see his reasoning before paying.
concerns: The only full record is published by a site that lists the same company and address as his own, and the FAQ calls it independent.
The guarantee gives more picks, never money, and season passes have none.
Streaks start on dates the seller chooses, and sales copy dollar figures assume $1,000 a pick.
Sales copy contradicts itself on years in business and on per day prices.
Free trials are tied to depositing at a recommended offshore sportsbook.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He runs a real business with a named operator, a public price list and a working checkout, and BBB lists one complaint, marked resolved. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because his only full record is graded by a site that lists the same company and address as his own.
How much does Jimmy Boyd cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 single best bets cost $39.99 to $59.97, day packs $74.97 to $99.97, all sports passes $49.95 for a day up to $1999.95 for 365 days, and season passes $599.95 to $999.97.
Does Jimmy Boyd have a verified record?

Not independently. SportsCapping publishes a dated archive of his picks with results and lead times, but SportsCapping lists the same operator as BoydsBets, and Watchdog has not matched him to a graded record.

For the money you get daily picks with written analysis, and on short packages a free repeat term if you lose, never cash. What is unproven is whether the picks beat the market over time at the lines you can actually get, since every record comes from the seller's own network.
